# read_A: p. 98 (rest of l. 3 to l. 5) and pp. 99–101 (images n99–n102), read from the images

## Lines and layout

- **p. 98 (n99)** has five lines. It is a leaf back with no ornament. The scan is rotated by about −1.8°, so I read it from a straightened copy. Headlines are at 114, 174, 231, 283 and 335.
  - I read 98.3 from the first syllable after `…སངས་རྒྱས་པར་འགྱུར་རོ༔` (x≈590), then 98.4 and 98.5.
  - My reading of these 2⅔ lines agrees with read_C (part 010) letter for letter. It was made independently from the image.
- **p. 99 (n100)** has five lines. It is a leaf front and opens with the horizontal swirl, then `༔`, a wide blank, and `༔`. I wrote this `༄༅༔ ༔`, as in 009/010. The scan is rotated by about +1.6°. Headlines are at 137, 192, 248, 302 and 358.
- **p. 100 (n101)** has five lines. It is a leaf back with no ornament. The scan is rotated by about −1.8°. Headlines are at 132, 186, 239, 295 and 346.
- **p. 101 (n102)** has five lines. It is a leaf front and opens `༄༅༔ ༔`. The scan is rotated by about +1.6°. Headlines are at 139, 191, 244, 298 and 355.
- In all I read 17⅓ print lines: the rest of 98.3, then 98.4–5, then 15 lines on pp. 99–101.

**Seam with B.** Line 101.5 ends `…འདི་སྐད་དོ༔ ཀྱེ་རིགས`. The last syllable is crushed against the frame and has no tsheg. p. 102 should open with `ཀྱི་བུ…`, which B is to confirm.

## Method

- I measured the skew of each image by maximising row-profile variance and cropped from rotated copies.
- I found the line bands from the row profile. Each line was cropped in four overlapping segments at ×2.6, then the doubtful places at ×4–×12 (LANCZOS). Some places I also cropped from the unrotated original, to avoid resampling.
- I checked every line end at ×6–×8 for a tsheg.
- Mid-line tshegs are often fused to the head bar in this print. Where the image cannot decide, I followed normal syllable division.

## [?] marks (4) and […] gaps (0)

| place | as written | candidates / why |
|---|---|---|
| 100.3 | `རིག་པའི་རྩལ[?]་དུ` | The stack is a compact ཙ-like letter with a small blob at the top left. That blob is probably the reduced ར-mgo, but the stack has only single height. Sense and the other recension both give `རྩལ`. If there is no ར, the print has a misprint `ཙལ`. |
| 101.1 | `༔རིག[?]་པ༔` (after `ཡན་ལག་`) | The first letter is a ར. Above it, touching the frame line, is a curled vowel mark that looks like a gi-gu (an e-vowel is possible), then ག, then པ. There is no ས. The other recension has `ཡན་ལག་རགས་པ` ("coarse limbs"), which is the only sense. As read, `རིག་པ` makes no sense here. If the mark is ink rather than a vowel, the print has `རག་པ`. See misprints. |
| 101.2 | `སྔར་གོང་དུ་བླ[?]་མས་གདམས་པའི` | I read `སྔར་གོང་དུ` from the image (ང as in the nearby `དང`). The stack after it is a box letter over a small subscript, which I took as བླ, followed by `མས`. `བླ་མས་གདམས་པའི` ("instructed by the lama") makes good sense. The other recension (`སྔར་གོམས་པའི`) gives no candidate for this stretch. |
| 101.4 | `གང་ཟག་བཟང་པོ[?]་ཉམས་ཀྱང` | After `བཟང` comes a narrow Z-like letter (ར, or a cramped པ) under the start of a naro, then a tall ཉ, then མ and ས. I took it as `པོ་ཉམས`. The other recension has `བཟང་པོ་ཡིན་ཀྱང`, but `ཡིན` does not fit these traces. The print's sense would be "a good person, even if [his practice] has declined". |

There are no `[…]` gaps.

## Readings checked closely (no mark)

- 99.1 `བོད` (×8): clearly ད, not ས. See misprints.
- 99.3 `ཇམས་པ` (×10–×12): a single-height ཇ-shaped letter, compared with the ཇ of 98.5 `འཇིགས`. There is no ར-mgo and no tall stack, so it is not `རྔམ`. See misprints.
- 99.3 `བྷནྡྷ`: two stacks with no tsheg between them (`བྷ` and `ནྡྷ`). Part 010 had `བྷན་དྷ` at 97.3.
- 99.4 `མཐོང་གཤོལ`: the ག is visible here. Compare `མཐོང་ཤོལ[?]` at 94.1, part 010.
- 99.5 `ཞལ་སྦྱོར་དུ་མངོན་སུམ་དུ`: the first `དུ` is clear (×7).
- 100.4 `ཡིན་གྱི།།` and 100.5 `ཡིན་གྱི་ངོ`: the stack's top letter is a closed box (I read ག). ཀ is not fully excluded, and the sense is the same either way. After the first one, two separate shad strokes are printed (×10), and I wrote them `།།`.
- 100.4 `མཐོང་བར་ལྟ་བུར`: a clear ར follows བ.
- 100.5 `མཚང་རིགས་ཏེ`: a full-size ས, then a separate ཏེ (not a stacked སྟེ).
- 101.3 `འཕྲད་བ་ལྟར` (×8): a closed box བ, as in the print's habit of `འཕྲོད་བ`.
- 101.3 `རང་གསལ་དུ་རང་གྲོལ་ལོ`: clear (×8).
- 101.4 `གའུ་རི`: a ག with no naro and no visible tsheg before `འུ`. Compare `གོའུ་རི་མ` at 98.4.

## Where the print differs in sense from the other recension (print followed)

- **98.3–4:** "…flees and does **not recognise** the yidam, and **there are those who** do not meet it" (`ངོ་མ་ཤེས་ཏེ་མ་འཕྲོད་པ་ཡོད་པས`). The other recension has "it is **possible** not to meet it" (`ངོ་མ་འཕྲོད་པ་སྲིད་པས`).
- **98.4–5:** the print **adds `སྨེ་མ་དང༔`** and has `ཕྲ་མེན་དང` (without མ). This is the same as part 010's note.
- **98.5:** "not recognising, **the terror grows greater**" (`འཇིགས་སྐྲག་ཆེ་རུ་འོངས་པས`). The other recension has `སྐྲག་ཏུ་འོང་བས`.
- **99.1:** the print lacks `མ་ཡེངས་པར་ཉོན་ཅིག` after `ཀྱེ་རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔`, as on day eleven (96.5).
- **99.2:** the faces are given as `ཞལ་གཡས་དཀར་བ༔ གཡོན་དམར་བ༔ དབུས་ལྗང་ནག་ཇམས་པ`, with `ཞལ` added. The sense is the same.
- **99.4:** the consort "embraces the body", **without `ཡབ་ཀྱི`**. The right hand embraces "**the father's** neck" (`ཡབ་ཀྱི་མགུལ`, which the other recension lacks), and the clause ends `འཁྱུད་པ༔`, where the other recension has `འཁྱུད་ཅིང`. The name is `ཀརྨ་ཀྲོ་ཏི་ཤྭ་རི` where the other recension has `ཀྲོ་ཏུ`.
- **99.3–4:** the last left-hand implement is `མཐོང་གཤོལ` (other recension `ཐོང་གཤོལ`). The middle one is `བྷནྡྷ`.
- **99.5:** `ཞལ་སྦྱོར་དུ་མངོན་སུམ་དུ` ("manifestly in union"). The other recension has `ཞལ་སྦྱོར་མངོན་སུམ་དུ`.
- **100.1:** `མ་དངངས་ཤིག` (the print's spelling). `ཁྱོད་རང་གི` is present here, unlike 98.1 in part 010.
- **100.2:** `དོན་ལ་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་དོན་ཡོད་གྲུབ་པ་དངོས་ཡིན་ནོ`. The print **lacks `ཡབ་ཡུམ`** and `ནི`. It also lacks `དུང་དུང` ("intensely") after `མོས་པ་དང་གུས་པ`, and `དུས` in `མཉམ་དུ` (the sense is the same).
- **100.3:** `བླ་མའི་གདམས་ངག་གི་རང་སྣང…`: the print has the genitive `གི`, where the other recension has the instrumental `གིས`.
- **100.4:** "they are liberated as if seeing a stuffed lion" ends a sentence (`གྲོལ་ལོ༔`). The other recension continues with `གྲོལ་ཏེ༔`. The print has `གསོབ་འདི་ལྟར` ("like this") where the other recension has `དེ་ལྟར`, and `སྐྲག་སྐྱེས་ཏེ` where it has `སྐྱེ་སྟེ`.
- **100.5:** `འཇིགས་པ་བྲལ་བ`, without `དང`. The sense is the same.
- **101.1:** `མཉམ་པར་ཆར་བའི་ཚེ` (`ཆར` without འ). The other recension has `མཉམ་པ་འཆར་བའི`. On `རིག[?]་པ`, see the [?] table.
- **101.2: real sense differences.**
  - Print: "recognising the yidam, **the clear light the lama instructed before** (`སྔར་གོང་དུ་བླ[?]་མས་གདམས་པའི་འོད་གསལ`)". The other recension has "the clear light **one has habituated to before** (`སྔར་གོམས་པའི`)".
  - Print: the two clear lights, mother and child, "**meet**" (`གཉིས་མ་བུ་འཕྲད་དེ`). The other recension has "**mingle**" (`མ་བུ་གཉིས་འདྲེས་ཏེ`).
  - Print: `ངོ་ཤེས་ནས`. The other recension has `ངོ་ཤེས་ཏེ`.
- **101.3:** "…like meeting a person one knew before: self-knowing, self-clear, **one is self-liberated**" (`རང་རིག་རང་གསལ་དུ་རང་གྲོལ་ལོ༔`). The other recension has `རང་རིག་རང་གསལ་རང་གྲོལ་དུ་འགྱུར་རོ༔`. Also print `འདིའི་ངོ་སྤྲོད` ("its pointing-out"), where the other recension has `འདིས`.
- **101.4:** `གང་ཟག་བཟང་པོ[?]་ཉམས་ཀྱང` ("even if a good person has declined") is unsure. The other recension has `ཡིན་ཀྱང` ("even a good person"). `གའུ་རི་བརྒྱད` is the print's spelling, beside `གོའུ` at 98.4 and the other recension's `ཀོའུ་རཱི`.
- **101.5:** `…རང་ལ་འཆར་དུ་འོང་ངོ༔ ཡང་ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་ནི༔`. The print closes a sentence here (`ངོ༔`), where the other recension has `ཤར་དུ་འོང་བས་༔`.

- **With a tsheg:** 98.3 `མ་` (then filler dots, left out), 99.1 `ལྡན་`, 99.4 `པས་`, 99.5 `འཇིགས་`, 100.1 `ལ་`, 100.2 `བསྒྲགས་`, 100.3 `དུ་`, 100.5 `ལག་`, 101.1 `རང་`, 101.2 `མ་`, 101.4 `སྣ་` (then filler dots, left out).
- **Ending in ༔:** 98.4, 99.3, 101.3.
- **No tsheg (fixes below):**
  - 98.5 `མིང` (→ 99.1 `ནས`, after the ornament)
  - 99.2 `དབུས` (the ས is crushed against the frame)
  - 100.4 `མི`
  - 101.5 `རིགས` (the seam with B)
- Filler dots inside `སྟོབ་…པ༔` (99.5) are left out, as at 97.4.
- **No missing mid-line tsheg** that I could establish. `གོའུ` (98.4) and `གའུ` (101.4) are written as printed.

## Fixes needed (`# fix:` lines)

The ornament joins follow the 010 convention, because the build strips the ornament before applying fixes.

```
# fix: ཚེ་འདས་ཀྱི་མིངནས => ཚེ་འདས་ཀྱི་མིང་ནས
# fix: གཡོན་དམར་བ༔ དབུསལྗང => གཡོན་དམར་བ༔ དབུས་ལྗང
# fix: སྐྱེས་ཏེ༔ མིགཅིག => སྐྱེས་ཏེ༔ མི་གཅིག
# fix: ཀྱེ་རིགསཀྱི => ཀྱེ་རིགས་ཀྱི
```

- The last fix is at the 101.5/102.1 seam and depends on B confirming that p. 102 opens with `ཀྱི`.
- No `པའཾ`, `ལཾ`, `ནམཁའ`, subscript-ས or -གས ligature forms occur on these pages.
- `ཁ་ཊྭཾ་ག` (99.3) keeps its anusvāra as printed.

## Suspected misprints

1. **99.1 `ནས་བོད་ལ་འདི་སྐད་དོ` → `བོས`.** This is the fixed formula `ཚེ་འདས་ཀྱི་མིང་ནས་བོས་ལ་འདི་སྐད་དོ`, which the print itself has at 96.5 and again at 101.5 (`བོས`, clear). The letter here is clearly ད. Only "calling" makes sense, and `བོད` could only be an unprefixed spelling of `འབོད`. Moderate certainty. Proposed: `# fix: ནས་བོད་ལ་འདི => ནས་བོས་ལ་འདི`. If the editor prefers to keep it as a spelling, it becomes a note only.
2. **99.3 `ལྗང་ནག་ཇམས་པ`.** The sense must be "fierce", `རྔམ(ས)་པ`, and the other recension has `རྔམ་པ`. ཇ for རྔ is a plausible cutting error, but the exact intended spelling (`རྔམ` or `རྔམས`) is not certain. **Kept, note only.** The editor may correct it to `རྔམས་པ`, with low to moderate certainty.
3. **101.1 `རིག[?]་པ`** for `རགས་པ` ("coarse"). Two changes would be needed (vowel and ས), so this is **kept, note only**.
4. **100.3 `རྩལ[?]`.** If the ར is absent, it is a misprint for `རྩལ`. See the [?] entry.
5. **Not misprints, kept:**
   - `དངངས` (the print's spelling throughout)
   - `ཆར་བ` (101.1)
   - `འཕྲད་བ` (101.3)
   - `མཚང་རིགས་ཏེ` (100.5; other recension `རིག་སྟེ`)
   - `གའུ་རི` beside `གོའུ་རི`
   - `ཀྲོ་ཏི`, `བྷནྡྷ`, `མཐོང་གཤོལ`, `ཀརྨ` (no long ཱ seen)
   - `།།` mid-sentence at 100.4
   - `ཆེ་རུ` (98.5)
   - 98.4–5 `ཕྲ་མེན་དང༔ སྨེ་མ་དང༔` (as in part 010's note)

- The ཀ/ག question at 100.4–5 is open, but the sense is the same either way.
